VFS fiasco and fraud

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
VFS is an international company with the parent company in Switzerland which handles many visa services globally. In SA VFS CEO and COO are India living in Dubai who secured the lucrative visa contract in 2014 after a dubious appointment. They are essentially providing a “post office” service for the Department of Home Affairs. Visa applicants now can only apply through VFS which costs them R1350 an application and an additional R20 to be informed via SMS when and if their application has been accepted.

Summary:
The website of VFS is appalling and although you are said to be able to appeal your rejected application online in fact you can’t and have to go in for another appointment which will cost another R1350. There is no tracking service so you have no idea when and if your application will be approved and you cannot follow anything up as VFS simply takes your application and returns it without being able to provide you with any answers. The services so bad VFS faces 3 or 4 litigations a week.
There have always been suspicions that the Gupta’s are involved but in fact it’s another “Indian India” company. The COO and CEO of the SA VFS contract are both India living in Dubai who have illegally subcontracted 80% of VFS services to another “Indian Indian” company called D and D Logan. Essentially they are divesting from VFS into D and D Logan either as a way of money laundering or as a way of avoiding paying tax showing that VFS is making a loss by taking out a legal contract with D and D Logan which makes no financial sense what so ever. All the rest of the VFS services like the IT and the legal and financial departments are in India.The only South Africans are the people working in the offices.
The story will look at victims of the VFS system, people who’s lives are on hold while they wait for their residents permits to be renewed which they are told can take up to a year and yet you cannot reapply until it has expired. Woman cannot register the births of their children because they are married to a South Africa but their residents permit has not been renewed, so there is no medical aid cover and they cannot travel with their babies. People cannot travel overseas for family weddings, or attend to their dying parents, because if they leave they will not be able to return to their families, jobs, and homes.
We have a whistle blower who can give us the inside on this illegal contract and the failings of VFS

Press Release:


Visa Vitriol
The Department of Home Affairs—described by some as ‘horror affairs’—introduced visa-handling service VFS in 2014 to streamline administration. But for foreigners - many of whom bring rare skills and investment into the country, applying to live and work in South Africa and complying with immigration regulations is still a nightmare experience. They report an expensive and cumbersome process in which the Department of Home Affairs allegedly rejects 40 percent of applications out of hand. Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


Nicole: We were so young when we fall in love and I also left my family and let everybody to be here with him, to be happy, my children are happy here and I still can’t get these papers right it’s just ridiculous
Script: Nicole and Stephan fell in love in Chile while he was on a school exchange program, she moved here 10 years ago, and every few years they go through the exhausting and expensive process of renewing her visa. She has been waiting for two years for her permanent residence. There are 10 of 1000’s of foreigners in a similar predicament
Maria “They are playing with our future they are playing with our business
Script: Maria, her husband and two children came to South Africa from Spain in 2009, investing 20 million rand in this Lodge. Two years ago they all applied for permanent residence
Maria “Last year in August I received my permanent residence approval. My husband doesn’t have his application finalised yet,
Devi “why but you both applied together “
Maria “My husband application is still in process with no feedback at all and for my kids, nothing
Script: The uncertainly is playing havoc with their lives, for 5 years Mano hasn’t been able to work or leave the country to visit family
This PhD academic hid her identity for fear of impacting her research; she started applying for her critical skills visa almost two years ago.
Sara “As an academic you are required to travel to bring the results to international conferences and in the last 2 years I just couldn’t do that, I am feeling very trapped and the international collaboration I have is being affected
Script: She can’t marry her fiancée, and her bank account is frozen regularly
Link: South Africa desperately needs investment and specialised skills but our immigration policy makes it extremely difficult for foreigners to honestly contribute to our economy
Script: The Act was amended in 2014, and Cape Town Immigration Attorney Gary Eisenberg says it was like the lights were switched off
Gary Eisenberg “Prior to the amendments our system was an open system…the hunt for international talent the inclusion of foreigners into the socio economic system of SA
Script: In June 2014 Home Affairs closed its doors to foreign applicants, forcing them to apply through an Intermediary
Links “VFS is a global visa facilitation service, they were appointed by the department of home affairs to handle things like work visas and permanent residency applications from foreigners, they receive documents and then pass it on to the department of home affairs
Script: Applicants can now apply online, book and pay for an appointment and have their biometrics taken which Home Affairs DG Mkuseli Apleni sees as a major innovation
Apleni “ How do we measure our success on this thing when we were not able to deliver we were taken to court day and night by people complaining about our services in the public space home affairs was called horror affairs”
Script: The biggest resentment is the fees VFS charges. IT specialist KD Mufunde paid close to R10 000 when applying for permanent residence for himself, his wife and child because he had to extend their visas at the same time. He paid R1 520 to Home Affairs and R8 100 to VFS.
KD “They charge you a lot of money that wasn’t charged before and they hand the application to Home affairs who are going to do the same process they have always done
Script: A year later KD’s application was declined and therefore his family’s as well. He paid VFS another R4 050 on appeal
Jiten “The service fees that we levy are duly approved by the department by way of our contract this program deals with foreigners living working studying in SA and it’s not a cost on the tax payer
Script: Jiten Vyas, COO of VFS Global, says they are entitled to charge a service fee for every person applying because applications are processed individually.
Links “It is a lucrative user pays business model, in 2015 VFS processed 135 000 applications that works out to R182 million rands in just one year
Script: All agree that VFS has certainly modernised the application process, but the IT issues are on-going explains this immigration agent who fears victimization of his clients if he reveals his identity:
Immigration Practitioner “The VFS website has got so many problems …when you apply on the website now you get error messages, contact the website manager and they will respond in 36 hours, you sit for 3 days and say sorry I cannot help you
Script: And the system had numerous problems in October. Part of the problem is that VFS Global’s IT system is not fully automated and there are ongoing issues with the transfer of data via the Bangladeshi hub to the Department of Home Affairs, says this insider:
Insider “VFS also lost a lot of information
Devi ”What do you mean lost information
Insider: “They purged information, they have lost biometrics and without a biometric the application’s incomplete
Devi” When will I find out as the applicant
Insider: When you try and enquire when you go to court when you throw your toys out the cot
Jiten- I am absolutely clear VFS Global has not lost any documentation, we collect documents we observe our security protocols the documents are scanned and electronically transmitted to the department
Immigration Practitioner “In reality documents still go missing you can submit a file there is a check list they scan it in their system and original gets sent to home affairs you still get rejections where they say there was not an a police clearance on there was not a medical certificate on then you go and check with VFS the scan is there the problem is at home affairs inside
Apleni “VFS had problems like Home Affairs had problems with our modernization problem but what we will do we will look at it, we improve day by day
Script: In 2014, 50% of all applications were rejected, because of poor adjudication and IT problems
Gary Eisenberg “Part of the rejection rate is caused by a great deal of arbitrariness no matter how you search for clarity you want to engage lawfully it is simply impossible to do so
Apleni “Adjudicators can make a mistake with this particular application that is why were even allowed an appeal process, if those adjudicators were saints we would not need an appeal process
Sara “The application was rejected on the basis that I needed to provide an extra letter this letter was not listed as a requirement on the application. When I ask VFS Global if this is even possible they say that home affairs can require any document at any time even if that was not listed.
Jiten “Our role is that of managing the administrative task. We are not privy to the decision and have no role what so ever in the decision making or the adjudication process.
Script: VFS and Home Affairs say the rate of rejections has dropped significantly since 2014 and the turn-around time for processing applications has improved, so we checked with a local attorney to see if that was their experience
Gary “we took a recent about a 3 month sweep and we looked at the rejection rate of about 37-40% so the figure has come down somewhat
Script: And the stress of these rejections is immense, which Tessa Graham will attest to. She is a corporate brand manager with a slew of international celebrity clients like Jamie Oliver; and has been living here with her son for the last 7 years; she was applying for a critical skills visa
Tessa Graham “We started the process in the middle of June 2015 and we finally submitted on Dec 5th 2015 and the cost of pulling all of that together was R75 000, the couriers, the submission costs, the costs to get my original college transcripts, my high school transcripts, the couriers from the FBI it adds up
Script: Tessa’s application was also rejected,
Tessa Graham” I was of course incredibly upset, my entire life, our home, our dogs, my son’s school, his friends, our community, could fall away
Script: She appealed, adding nothing new except a covering letter from her lawyer.
Tessa Graham “I thought that there would be no issues and that I would have my one visa go into the next visa but that wasn’t the case so the choice that I had to make was, was I going to run to the United Kingdom and get a tourist visa to be able to come back that would have cost us another R40 000
Script: Time also ran out for Nicole despite being assured by VFS that the 9 months on her spousal visa would be adequate.
Nicole “We were struggling a bit financially to get the papers from Chile
Stephan “We realised we needed to have R6 000 cash to spend on the next application
Script: Before she could extend her spousal visa she needed a letter of good cause - it’s the explanation for why your visa lapsed. It required travelling to Cape Town every 2 weeks, leaving home at 4 am to get her paper stamped to say she could stay another two weeks.
Nicole “Sorry your letter of good cause needs to pass through 5 signatures, if one person says no you definitely got a no a rejection letter.
Script: Four months later her letter was rejected - it was not good enough. An appeal takes 8 months. Nicole was trapped, her mother is ill with cancer in Chile and if she leaves she will break up the family. She opted to pay a fine fearing a criminal record. She was locked in a holding cell while they processed the paper work
Nicole “I am not a criminal why did I need to be there in the cell with all these criminals it was just horrible
Apleni “Home affairs is still not out of the woods, what I am saying to you is that if you compare a 2016 Home Affairs to the 2010 it is not the same
Script: Maria’s husband and children received their permanent residence two weeks after this interview – the DG said critical skills, work, and business visas took priority. He also undertook to investigate Nicole’s case. But many foreigners have just given up, taking their skills and money elsewhere. Tessa finally got a two year visa.
Devi “Can you run this gauntlet again”
Tessa “Offfh I don’t know if I could”.

There is no tracking service so you have no idea when and if your application will be approved and you cannot follow anything up as VFS simply takes your application and returns it without being able to provide you with any answers. The services so bad VFS faces 3 or 4 litigations a week. There have always been suspicions that the Gupta’s are involved but in fact it’s another “Indian India” company. The COO and CEO of the SA VFS contract are both India living in Dubai who have illegally subcontracted 80% of VFS services to another “Indian Indian” company called D and D Logan. Essentially they are divesting from VFS into D and D Logan either as a way of money laundering or as a way of avoiding paying tax showing that VFS is making a loss by taking out a legal contract with D and D Logan which makes no financial sense what so ever. All the rest of the VFS services like the IT and the legal and financial departments are in India.The only South Africans are the people working in the offices. The story will look at victims of the VFS system, people who’s lives are on hold while they wait for their residents permits to be renewed which they are told can take up to a year and yet you cannot reapply until it has expired. Woman cannot register the births of their children because they are married to a South Africa but their residents permit has not been renewed, so there is no medical aid cover and they cannot travel with their babies. People cannot travel overseas for family weddings, or attend to their dying parents, because if they leave they will not be able to return to their families, jobs, and homes. We have a whistle blower who can give us the inside on this illegal contract and the failings of VFS
